Subject: RFP Q4 - detailed regional data location matrix request

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking our initial call today. As part of our RFP, procurement has asked for a single-page matrix that clearly documents:
- Where customer content and request/response logs are stored (data plane) for Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) options across EU/US/APAC;
- Whether control plane metadata and auditing logs ever leave the customer region;
- KMS options (Redwood-owned vs customer BYOK) and key locality;
- Any known model availability differences by region (e.g., certain model variants only in US for latency/cost reasons);
- Contractual commitments (e.g., EEA-only processing, data deletion timelines).

Could you attach that matrix and call out any hard constraints we need to surface to our legal/security teams? We have a hard requirement to identify any processing that might occur outside the EEA for EU patients.

Appreciate it — goal is to include your deliverable in the RFP by EOD Friday.

Best,

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask and the context. Attached is a concise regional matrix (attached: northbridge-2025-regional-data-matrix.xlsx) and a short one-pager that summarizes our options. High-level points up-front: 

- Hosted API (Redwood-managed):
  • Data plane (requests and generated content) is stored in the region you select (US/EU/APAC) for active serving. We support region pinning per-account to keep primary storage in-region.
  • Control plane metadata (billing, usage analytics) is by default stored in Redwood control plane; we can restrict certain audit log exports to region or provide redaction/aggregation by contract.
  • KMS: Redwood-managed keys by default (global), but we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with keys provisioned in customer-chosen cloud KMS in EU/US/APAC. BYOK ensures ciphertext keys never leave selected region.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  • You get capacity provisioned in a single region/zone you select — data plane remains in that region.
  • Optional network isolation and private peering.
  • We can offer contractual EEA-only processing for Dedicated with audit evidence and region-only backup policies.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  • Control plane can be run as a private control plane inside your VPC or we provide an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments.
  • For on-prem deployments, no outbound traffic to Redwood control plane is required; all data and logs stay on customer infrastructure by default.

Model availability and nuances:
- We maintain a curated model catalog. Some latest experimental variants are initially hosted in US regions for rollout speed; we replicate stable variants to EU/APAC within 2–6 weeks based on demand.
- When using region-replicated models, performance characteristics (latency, batching) are equivalent; however, some cost/quantization variants may only be offered on Dedicated in certain regions. We call these out in the matrix.

Contractual commitments and evidence:
- We support EEA-only processing terms in the DPA and will sign SCCs.
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II reports, penetration test summaries, and region-scoped audit logs. For control-plane metadata that must not leave region, we offer a configurable retention/export pipeline and can redact PII at the ingestion layer.

I attached the matrix and the DPA/SCC summary (redwood-dpa-sccs-2025.pdf). Quick question: when you say 'EEA-only processing for EU patients' — do you need a technical guarantee (no cross-region replication at any time) or a contractual guarantee with specified exceptions for disaster recovery? That will influence whether Dedicated or Private is required.

Happy to jump on a quick 30-minute call with your security team if helpful — propose Thu 14:00–15:00 CEST or Fri 09:00–10:00 CEST.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt

1) For Hosted API with BYOK, confirm whether metadata (request timestamps, prompt fingerprints, error traces) may still be routed through a global control plane hosted in the US for orchestration. We need to know if any metadata elements are persisted outside EEA even with BYOK.

Also, is there an option to route billing/usage telemetry to our own telemetry endpoint (so we can retain logs in-region)? If not, can Redwood provide a time-limited export of raw audit logs per month?

We are trying to determine whether Hosted API (with contractual controls) will meet our policy or whether we must insist on Dedicated or Private.

Hi Daniel / Sophie — Karthik on the infra team here, a few technical clarifications to make the decision easier:

1) Hosted + BYOK: BYOK ensures customer data at rest is encrypted with keys you control in the region. Control-plane metadata (routing tables, job scheduling) is lightweight and may be processed by our control-plane services; however, we can configure the control plane to operate regionally for your account (EEA-only) as part of a Dedicated or Enterprise Private package. When configured regionally, audit logs and usage summaries can be stored in-region and only aggregated out-of-region in redacted form if you authorize.

2) Backups: For Dedicated, cross-region backups are not performed by default unless you opt into disaster recovery replication. We can provision geo-fenced backups (EEA-only) and encrypt backups with customer KMS keys provisioned in your cloud account.

3) Telemetry & exports: Redwood supports pushing usage/audit logs to customer-owned S3 buckets or object storage endpoints in the region. We provide a scheduled export (daily or monthly) and can also create an on-demand export for audits. If you want to receive telemetry in near-real-time, we can set up an event-forwarding pipeline to your telemetry endpoint behind a private endpoint.

4) Model availability: Some new model variants (alpha/bleeding-edge) are launched in our US regions for iterative testing. For production SLAs we replicate stable models to EU/APAC. If you require guarantees that a given model never leaves region, Private (on-prem) or Dedicated with regional-only replication is the recommended path.

I attached a short ops note in the matrix describing where each artifact (request logs, KV cache snapshots, model weights, ephemeral inference cache) resides by deployment mode. Happy to add any extra columns you need.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
